property_summary: For every interfaceId, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true for IERC165's id and for IAccessControl's id when queried accordingly (i.e., supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) == true), while the mutant that always returns false will return false for at least that interface id.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference C reports true when asked about IAccessControl's interface id (type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) while the mutant that always returns false will report false for that id, so the universal property is: calling supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) must return true; the mutant breaks that.

For every bytes4 id, calling supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) on the reference C returns true (it reports support for IAccessControl); the mutant that always returns false will return false for that interface id, violating this rule for some inputs.

For every interfaceId the reference contract C reports support for IAccessControl (i.e. supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) == true), while the mutant may report false for that same interfaceId because it removed the explicit IAccessControl check.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference C reports support for IAccessControl's interfaceId exactly as (supportsInterface(interfaceId) || false) — in particular the reference always returns true for interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, while the mutant that only defers to super may return false for that interfaceId; thus there exists an interfaceId (the IAccessControl id) that the reference accepts but the mutant rejects.

For every bytes4 interfaceId the reference C returns true for the IAccessControl interface id (type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) when queried via supportsInterface, while the mutant that delegates only to super may return false for that specific interface id — therefore the reference always reports support for IAccessControl but the mutant may not.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference C always returns true when queried for IAccessControl's interfaceId (type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) via supportsInterface, but the mutant that removes the explicit IAccessControl check may return false for that specific interfaceId—so the property is: supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) always returns true on the correct contract.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference contract's supportsInterface never reverts and for the IAccessControl interface id it must return true; the mutant that omitted the IAccessControl check can return false for that id, so there exists an interfaceId (specifically type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) where reference returns true but mutant may return false.

For every interfaceId, the correct contract returns true iff interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or super.supportsInterface(interfaceId) is true; the mutant inverts the check and will return false for IAccessControl.interfaceId even though the reference returns true.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference contract returns true when interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or when its super supports the interface; the mutant flips the equality check and therefore will return false for interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId while the reference returns true for that input.
